findings.title: Revoke locally stored recovery codes after replacing them in user storage
findings.body: When a federated user already has recovery codes stored in Keycloak, a successful user-storage update leaves that existing credential untouched. This is particularly relevant when upgrading, since the required action previously always stored recovery codes in Keycloak. Credential validation can fall back to the local provider when external validation fails, so regenerating codes now leaves the old local codes usable alongside the new set. Remove the existing local recovery-code credential after successfully replacing it in user storage, and cover this migration/regeneration case in a test.

findings.title: Remove exhausted credentials from their actual storage
findings.body: The new lookup can return a credential owned by an external user-storage provider, but the exhaustion branch below still passes its ID to removeStoredCredentialById, which only deletes Keycloak-stored credentials. For a provider that keeps its credential record configured after consuming the final code, the exhausted record therefore remains. If the user abandons the subsequent regeneration page, the next login selects that record and RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean calls getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get() on an empty Optional, preventing login. Disable/remove external credentials through their provider instead. The new test fixture never consumes codes, so an exhaustion test with a stateful provider is needed to exercise this path.
